entry.title: Ubisoft Details Rendering Pipeline for Assassin's Creed Shadows
entry.content:
GDC Videos | youtube.com | source

During a GDC 2025 presentation, Technical Architect Nicolas Lopez outlined the rendering advancements in Assassin's Creed Shadows and the evolution of the Anvil engine. The engine has transitioned to a monorepo architecture to streamline development and features enhanced scalability to support massive, systemic open worlds.

The architecture relies on a GPU-driven pipeline and a specialized "Database" system for efficient data sharing between the CPU and GPU. Performance across vast environments is maintained through a hierarchy of LOD techniques, including point clouds for mass imposter rendering and a micro-polygon geometry pipeline for efficient rasterization.

entry.content:

The gaming industry is comprised of four distinct sectors: single-player casual, single-player core, mobile/casual live service, and core live service. The mobile and casual live service market functions as a math-driven business focused on user acquisition and lifetime value via gacha mechanics, whereas core PC and console markets rely on cosmetic sales and gameplay-integrated randomness.

This divergence in monetization necessitates different company structures and design philosophies. While math-based mechanics drive success in mobile gaming, the core audience generally requires a focus on cosmetic items and gameplay-focused randomness to maintain engagement.
